hypothesis.statement: LoadWorldDone, not StartWorldLoad, is the class's best natural experiment and it kills the prologue-shadow explanation on its own. Its aligned view at +0x18 shows the `lis` emitted AFTER the frame is fully set up (`stwu r1,-40(r1)` at +0x8, `stmw r26,16(r1)` at +0xc), so there is NO pre-prologue shadow hoist at all and r28 is ALREADY saved when the `addi` issues - and our build still writes `addi r0,r3,LO` + `mr r28,r0` while the target writes `addi r28,r3,LO`. That is a cleaner refutation of the save-timing/shadow account than the `#pragma scheduling off` construct used on MBOX_BGLoadModelStart, because it is natural codegen with no pragma in the tree. Whatever forces the r0 detour is therefore not shadow occupancy and not save timing; it is an allocator decision about whether the ADDR16_LO result may be written directly into a live callee-saved web.
